review_output: {"summary":"Exact arithmetic checks out. The common-scale threshold, eligibility clip, early exit and [S,T) window are equivalent to the reference. The read-model reconciliation is correct, including the 27017/27018 boundary. I found no correctness regression. Remaining concerns are performance evidence at the permitted scale bound, unbounded aggregate work, and test and benchmark repeatability.","findings":[{"area":"performance","severity":"MAJOR","issue":"The 2s budget is unproven at the scale sizes the 16384-bit bound permits.","impact":"Benchmarks use durations 900–1100ms, so the scale is only a few thousand bits. Real 5s samples can reach about 7,200 bits, and the bound allows 16,384. Each completedAt pass touches N BigInts, runs about 54 times, and prepareSegments allocates three scaled BigInts per row. Latency and memory at the bound are unmeasured and may approach or exceed 2s.","file":"src/lib/live-viewing-evidence.ts","recommended_fix":"Benchmark 10000 segments with durations spread over 1..5000ms and at the bound. Then either lower MAX_RATIONAL_SCALE to a measured safe value or document the measured ceiling.","required_test":"Benchmark: 10000 rows, varied durations 1..5000ms and a scale just under the bound; assert under 2s with a result identical to the reference.","confidence":0.5,"evidence":"MAX_RATIONAL_SCALE = 1<<16384; performance-check.mjs cases use 900+i%201 durations; completedAt does multi-BigInt work per segment per binary-search step."},{"area":"performance","severity":"MINOR","issue":"Work limits are per person only. Stop the completion loop once completionLimit is set.","required_test":"Cohort of many persons with large histories: completion and order become limit_exceeded while attendance and average are preserved, and the call finishes in budget.","confidence":0.6,"evidence":"viewingMetrics loops all persons calling firstCompletionTime; on limit_exceeded it only sets completionLimit and continues."},{"area":"tests","severity":"MINOR","issue":"The unit suite never exercises the common-LCM path with mixed coprime segment durations.","impact":"Existing multi-segment tests use equal durations, so the scale/lcm and per-segment rate arithmetic is checked only by the out-of-tree random benchmark.
